answer: Sybil resistance here is stake-weighted attestation: each agent locks scarce collateral, and every identity it spawns draws from that same bond instead of minting fresh voting weight. Reaching the summit of trust needs a crystal record of honest past votes, since the ledger traces each new identity back through the willow of its parent's reputation. Splitting into clones divides one bond, never multiplies it, and double-voting is slashed. To sway a decision an attacker must buy over a third of all stake — costly and self-defeating.
